caption: The drawing depicts a single large, metallic tub with a rounded, high back and a wide rim. The tub has a weathered, dull bluish-gray surface with patches of brown and rust that indicate signs of wear and oxidation. The front and sides of the tub angle slightly outward as they extend downward, and the base flares out into a flat, circular support. The interior line of the tub is visible at the top edge, and there appears to be a handle or small projection on each side. The composition is centered on a plain, off-white or beige background, and the main object is framed by a thin, rectangular red line. In the lower left corner, there is a small inset drawing of the tub, rendered in a simple outline style with measurement lines indicating the tub’s width of 23 inches and height of 21.5 inches. The names “Vincent P. Rosel” and “Gordon M. Saltar” are written in fine text at the bottom right of the frame.
title: Bath Tub
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
